Health Insurance Claim Rejection: 15 Real Reasons & How to Prevent Them

By Hari Kotian | Published on 2026-07-25

Health insurance claims in India have an average rejection rate that concerns every policyholder. Understanding why claims are rejected is the best prevention strategy. In this guide, I cover the 15 most common reasons — and what you can do right now to protect your coverage.

1. Non-Disclosure of Pre-Existing Diseases (PED)

Failing to declare a pre-existing condition like diabetes or hypertension at the time of buying the policy is the single most common reason for claim denial. Insurers can void the policy if a PED is discovered later.

Prevention:

Always declare all known medical conditions honestly at the time of application. If you've already bought a policy without disclosure, consider a portability application to a new insurer with full disclosure.

2. Waiting Period Not Completed

Health policies have waiting periods — typically 30 days for general illness, 2-4 years for specific diseases like cataracts or hernia, and 48 months for pre-existing conditions.

Prevention:

Read your policy document carefully. Plan medical procedures after waiting periods are completed. For planned surgeries, buy coverage well in advance.

3. Room Rent Capping Violation

Many policies restrict room type (e.g., shared room only) or cap room rent at 1% of sum insured. Claiming for an upgraded room can result in proportional deduction or full rejection.

Prevention:

Choose a policy with a generous room rent limit or no cap. If upgrading, check the proportional deduction clause before admission.

4. Treatment at a Non-Network Hospital

If your policy is a cashless-only plan, going to a hospital outside the insurer's network will result in rejection for reimbursement claims.

Prevention:

Always verify your hospital is in the insurer's network for cashless claims. Keep reimbursement claim documents ready if using a non-network hospital.

5. Self-Funded or Outpatient Expenses

Day-care procedures, doctor consultations, diagnostic tests without hospitalization, and dental treatment (unless specified) are not covered under standard health policies.

Prevention:

Buy a top-up plan that covers OPD. Read your policy to understand what qualifies as a valid hospitalization claim.

6. Intentional Non-Disclosure (Fraud)

If the insurer finds that a material fact was withheld with the intent to deceive, they can reject the claim and cancel the policy entirely — even if the illness is unrelated.

Prevention:

Be 100% honest on the proposal form. Material facts include habits (smoking, alcohol), profession risks, and all medical history.

7. Claim Outside Policy Term

If the policy has lapsed due to non-payment of premium, any claim made after the lapse date is rejected.

Prevention:

Set renewal reminders. Use auto-pay to avoid accidental lapse. If lapsed, use the free-look or revival period to reinstate.

8. Sub-Limit Exceeded

Many policies impose sub-limits on specific treatments — e.g., cataract surgery capped at Rs. 40,000 or mental health treatment at Rs. 20,000. Claiming above the cap leads to short-settlement.

Prevention:

Choose policies without sub-limits for critical treatments. Read the coverage table to know exact caps before undergoing treatment.

9. Pre-Authorization Delay

For cashless claims, insurers require pre-authorization before admission. Delaying this request beyond the hospital's internal deadline can result in rejection.

Prevention:

Request cashless authorization at least 24-48 hours before a planned admission. For emergencies, authorize within 24 hours of admission.

10. Incorrect or Incomplete Documentation

Missing hospital discharge summary, incorrect diagnosis codes, unsigned documents, or incomplete investigation reports are among the top administrative reasons for claim delays and rejections.

Prevention:

Collect all documents before discharge: discharge summary, final bill, investigation reports, prescription slips, and payment receipts. Review them before submitting.

11. Cosmetic or Elective Procedures

Weight loss treatments, plastic surgery (unless due to accident), hair transplant, and IVF are excluded from standard health insurance.

Prevention:

Read the exclusions list before buying. If you anticipate such treatments, look for specialized add-on covers or riders.

12. War, Nuclear Risk, or Intentional Self-Injury

Standard policies exclude claims arising from war, nuclear contamination, riots, and self-harm. Claims linked to these causes are automatically rejected.

Prevention:

These exclusions are standard and unavoidable. Ensure other aspects of your policy are comprehensive to cover everyday risks.

13. Domiciliary Hospitalization Not Qualified

Treatment taken at home is covered only if it meets specific criteria — e.g., the patient cannot be moved to a hospital, or nursing care is required at home. Simply preferring home treatment is not sufficient.

Prevention:

File domiciliary claims only when supported by a doctor certificate stating medical necessity for home treatment. Keep all prescriptions and logs.

14. Fraud or Misrepresentation

Filing a claim with inflated bills, duplicate claims, or altered documents is considered fraud. Insurers share data via CIS (Claim Information Sharing) platform, making duplicate claims easy to detect.

Prevention:

Never inflate bills or file duplicate claims. Keep all originals safe and submit only certified copies to the insurer.

15. Illness/Accident During Waiting Period After Renewal

If you switch insurers and don't port your continuity benefits, a condition that was waiting under the old policy restarts its waiting period under the new policy.

Prevention:

Always use portability to transfer your policy when switching. Continuity benefits for pre-existing conditions must be ported; don't let them lapse.
